description: Rainbond is an open-source container platform that requires no Kubernetes expertise. Its core capabilities are 100% open source.  It abstracts away infrastructure complexity and provides a unified way to deploy and manage business applications, AI-generated projects, open-source AI software, and large language model services. AI helps teams deploy

summary.one_liner: Rainbond is an open-source container platform that lets users build, deploy, and manage applications on Kubernetes through a graphical interface without needing deep Kubernetes expertise.
summary.what_it_does: Rainbond deploys applications from source code, container images, Docker Compose, Helm charts, or application templates. It provides a graphical console for managing application dependencies, access, upgrades, and rollbacks. It includes an application template system and marketplace with one-click install and upgrade, plus customer environment replication. It supports offline package export and import, and delivery across multiple environments and clusters. The README says it targets private, internal-network, and offline deployments, as well as Xinchuang (domestic hardware/software) adaptation and x86-to-ARM migration validation. It is also positioned for deploying AI-generated projects, open-source AI software, and large language model services, on your own servers or Kubernetes clusters.
use_cases: deploy open-source apps such as Dify or RAGFlow
privately deploy AI and LLM services
replicate application delivery to customer environments
how_to_run: Confirm the host is Linux or macOS (recommended at least 2 CPU / 8GB RAM / 50GB disk)
Deploy your first app from the console
notable: Graphical interface for Kubernetes application delivery with no K8s expertise required
Application-level abstraction with topology, dependencies, upgrades and rollbacks
Offline package export/import and one-click install/upgrade for private delivery
Related projects include rainbond-console, rainbond-ui, rainbond-operator, and builder
caveats: Recommended minimum of 2 CPU / 8GB RAM / 50GB disk, and the quick install is documented for Linux or macOS only
The README says the core capabilities are open source, and the repository is licensed under the Rainbond Open Source License, which is Apache 2.0 with additional conditions
Rainbond Cloud is offered as a hosted option; the README does not describe its terms
